chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba, from Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Shall I inform you of the root of Islam, its branch, its peak, and its high point?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Its root is salat, its branch is zakat, and its peak and high point is jihad in the way of God. Shall I inform you of the doors of goodness? Fasting is a shield.'

key_terms.أَصْل: Root/foundation — the indispensable base of a structure or system
key_terms.جُنَّة: Shield/protection — fasting as a defense against sin and spiritual harm
key_terms.ذِرْوَة: Peak/summit — the highest point, denoting excellence and supremacy
key_terms.سَنَام: Hump/high point (literally the camel's hump, the highest part of its back) — used metaphorically for the pinnacle
key_terms.فَرْع: Branch — a dependent but essential extension of the root

ai.seo_question: What is the root, branch, and peak of Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) describes the hierarchical structure of Islam's pillars to a companion named Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz. Using an organic metaphor of a tree — root, branch, and high point — the Imam places salat (prayer) as the foundation, zakat as its branch, and jihad in the way of God as the loftiest expression. He then adds that fasting serves as a protective shield, presenting the major acts of worship as an interconnected, ascending structure. This classification reflects early Shia understanding of worship as a hierarchy, where the outward acts support and crown one another.
